skills.summary: Places each architectural component in a PAID quadrant by change activity and Code Health, and estimates the outcomes and team ROI of uplifting the components to address first.

Turns CodeScene's uplift targets into a prioritized refactoring backlog: why each file, where to start, who to involve, the risks to plan for, the estimated outcome, and a refactoring spec to hand to a coding agent.

The project's truck factor and what leaves with each key person: CodeScene's off-boarding risks, the uplift targets that depend on one person, the components led by one person, and the knowledge already lost.

The architecture the commit history reveals: implicit dependencies between components, the coordination they force between people, and how hard each is to break given the Code Health of the coupled code.

A one-page summary of every CodeScene project you can access, for technical leaders and managers: what works well, where attention is needed, and how much of the code is AI-optimal, by hotspot Code Health.

How a project's developers use the local Code Health MCP: safeguard checks, degradations prevented, Code Health uplifts, the trend over a year, the most active users, which tools they rely on, and which installations are out of date.

How Code Health safeguards work on a project's pull requests: how often the review catches an issue, how many findings authors fix rather than ignore or suppress, whether each pull request maintained Code Health, the trend week by week, and the same per developer and per pull request.

Whether the code added to a project over the last month is healthy and AI-ready: new code per module and package with its median and lowest Code Health, an alert for new technical debt, the share that is AI-optimal, line coverage when the project has it, and who to involve.
